text: **Work Summary – Julia, Cryptographer**   *Period: Q3 2024*  This quarter centered on advancing our post-quantum migration roadmap while hardening existing key management protocols. I led the integration of CRYSTALS-Kyber-1024 into our internal messaging service, reducing handshake latency by 18% compared to the previous NTRU-based prototype. The implementation passed all NIST ACVP test vectors, and I documented edge cases around rejection sampling under low-entropy environments.  I also performed a cryptographic audit of our Ed25519 signature usage across distributed storage nodes. Discovered a nonce-reuse vulnerability in one legacy client (due to faulty random source) and coordinated a patch within 48 hours. This incident prompted a review of our randomness generation practices, leading to a new policy requiring periodic reseeding from hardware TRNGs.  Collaborating with the protocol team, I designed a threshold BLS scheme for validator consensus. The scheme reduces signature size by 60% over current Schnorr multi-sigs, with formal security proofs under the random oracle model. I authored the specification and ran simulation tests for up to 100 nodes with network partitions; results show robust liveness under Byzantine conditions.  On the research side, I published an internal paper on practical side-channel countermeasures for lattice-based KEMs. The work proposes a masked encoding of polynomial coefficients that cuts EM leakage by ~40% without significant performance overhead. Peer review is ongoing, and I plan to present it at the next company-wide security summit.  Finally, I mentored two junior cryptographers, guiding them through code reviews and threat modeling exercises. One has since taken ownership of the TLS 1.3 cipher suite configuration module.  Next quarter: focus on zero-knowledge proof integration for identity verification and further optimization of Kyber on constrained IoT devices. Decentralized identity will only thrive if we treat privacy as a primitive, not an add-on. I continue to advocate for minimal data exposure and robust cryptographic defaults.
